claims.text: The unmodified Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr alloy is single-phase BCC.
The BCC alloy exhibits asymmetric XRD peaks indicative of dendritic versus interdendritic micro-segregation.
The unmodified alloy has low room-temperature fracture strain.
The baseline alloy's low fracture strain is caused by micro-segregation and the absence of secondary-phase reinforcement.
Adding approximately 4 at.% Cr induces precipitation of a complex multicomponent Laves phase.
The Cr-induced Laves phase occupies approximately 4 vol% of the alloy.
The Cr-induced Laves phase has a reticulated, interconnected morphology.
The interconnected Laves-phase network forces cracks onto tortuous paths through crack deflection and branching.
Crack deflection and branching increase the energy required for fracture and impede crack extension.
Cr solute atoms produce lattice distortion in the BCC matrix.
Cr addition causes a measurable contraction of the BCC lattice parameter.
Cr-induced lattice contraction increases the Peierls stress.
The increased Peierls stress contributes to solid-solution hardening.
A reticulated Laves-phase network increases room-temperature fracture strain relative to the unmodified alloy.
Reticulated Laves-phase formation is favored only while the Cr-induced lattice contraction remains within a critical range.
Contraction beyond the critical range causes the Laves phase to transition from an interconnected network to discrete particles.
Discrete Laves-phase particles are less effective than a reticulated network at impeding crack extension.

contradictions.description: The boundary predicts that exceeding the contraction range may legitimately produce discrete Laves particles, whereas the falsification rule treats formation of discrete particles after 4 at.% Cr addition as falsifying without conditioning that result on whether the contraction boundary was exceeded.
